overview: Global (2026) roadmap for solo and small-team game developers. Focuses on the full lifecycle: from engine mastery and game design theory to publishing on Steam/consoles and leveraging AI for asset generation.

steps.title: 1. Game Design Foundations & Psychology
steps.description: Understanding why games are fun and how to keep players engaged.
subtopics: The 8 Types of Fun (LeBlanc's Taxonomy): Fellowship, Expression, Challenge, etc.
The 'Flow State': Balancing difficulty vs. player skill
Core Loops: Action → Feedback → Reward
Mechanics, Dynamics, and Aesthetics (MDA Framework)
Game Feel & Juiciness: Screenshake, particles, and hit-stop
Level Design: Signposting, pacing, and player guidance

steps.title: 2. Engine Mastery (Pick One)
steps.description: The technical backbone of your game. Master the API and the scripting language.
subtopics: Unity: C# scripting, Universal Render Pipeline (URP), Prefabs, Scriptable Objects
Godot: GDScript/C#, Scene-tree system, open-source workflow, 2D/3D nodes
Unreal Engine: C++, Blueprints (Visual Scripting), Nanite/Lumen, Physics
Version Control for Games: Git LFS (Large File Storage) or Perforce
Optimization: Draw calls, batching, and memory management for low-end hardware

steps.title: 3. Technical Art & Asset Pipelines
steps.description: Creating the visual and auditory experience.
subtopics: 2D Art: Pixel art (Aseprite), Vector (Illustrator), or Hand-drawn
3D Art: Modeling (Blender), Texturing (Substance), Rigging/Animation
Shaders & VFX: Visual Effect Graph, HLSL/GLSL shaders
Audio Engineering: Sound effects (SFX), Ambient loops, Spatial 3D audio
UI/UX for Games: Diegetic vs. non-diegetic HUDs, controller remapping

steps.title: 4. AI for Indie Developers (The 2026 Edge)
steps.description: Using AI to bridge the 'Asset Gap' and speed up development.
subtopics: Generative Art: Stable Diffusion for concept art and seamless textures
Procedural Generation: AI-driven noise for infinite terrain and dungeon layouts
AI NPCs: Large Language Models (LLMs) for dynamic dialogue and behavior trees
Code Assistance: Cursor or Copilot for writing complex physics math or boilerplate
AI Voiceovers: ElevenLabs or similar for high-quality temp (or final) dialogue

steps.title: 5. Marketing & The Business of Indie Games
steps.description: Ensuring your game actually gets played (and paid for).
subtopics: Steam Page Optimization: Capsules, trailers (the 'First 5 Seconds' rule), and tags
Wishlist Strategy: Building a community via Discord, Twitter, and TikTok
Festivals: Entering Steam Next Fest and Indie Megabooth
Monetization: Premium vs. F2P, DLC strategy, and localization (LQA)
Publishing: Solo-publishing vs. seeking a publisher (Devolver, Team17, etc.)

steps.title: Capstone Projects: Indie Dev Portfolio
steps.description: Projects that prove you can finish a game, not just a prototype.

projects.name: The 'Game Jam' Winner
projects.description: A polished 5-minute experience built within a 48-hour constraint. Focus on a single, unique mechanic.

projects.name: Procedural Dungeon Crawler
projects.description: A top-down or first-person game with randomized levels, item loot tables, and simple AI enemies.

projects.name: Multi-Platform Narrative Experience
projects.description: A story-heavy game with branching dialogue, dynamic audio, and support for both Mouse/Keyboard and Controller.
